title: A Saigon roundabout, a taxi, and a rooftop bar remembered
description: A five-storey modern block at a traffic circle, rooftop billboards for Bireley's orange drink, a display wall of national flags on the island below, and a blue-and-cream Saigon taxi crossing in front. "This picture is of Saigon because that is a Saigon Taxi. Not sure what the building is but I would guess it's a restaurant hotel." The frame set off two memories of Stanton: "One time in Saigon, I was on a bar on a roof with Zukowski, Stanton and there was war going on all around us. It was one of my last days in Saigon." And after the war: "Stanton is from New York. One time Stanton came into my machine shop in LA on Western Blvd and we went into King Henry the 8th topless club to eat."
researchNotes: Larry's caption of 2026-09-05 (giscus-vn-0081-c18308075.json). The building is his guess and is left unidentified. The survey read the flag wall on the island as a public tally board for the central-Vietnam flood relief campaign, which ran in the winter of 1964–65 — a machine reading of partial Vietnamese text, so a dating hypothesis only, not adopted. The Stanton material changed that man's record substantially (data/people/pfc-stanton.json): he is real, from New York, and in touch after the war — but no longer the man in VN-0026. The rooftop bar with 'war going on all around us' in his last days in Saigon is undated and unplaced.
